documents.title: Release request and acceptance worksheet
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. All systems, people, measurements and records are invented.
Request HBR-14, 2026-07-02. Owner: replay-platform-demo.
Requested action: make candidate Cobalt the default parser for the existing nightly harbor-48 sandbox replay job. The request does not change production traffic, the production parser, or the sandbox's permitted endpoints. The prior default is baseline Larch. The requested review concerns this bounded job change only.

ACCEPTANCE WORKSHEET, fixed before the comparison
Required bundle: harbor-48 revision 2, exactly 48 scenarios.
Functional gate: all 48 candidate runs accepted; zero wrong-record updates; zero writes to a non-sandbox destination.
Operational gate: sandbox endpoint restriction remains enabled; a rollback to Larch must have been exercised successfully in the same runner configuration.
If a required item fails, the default remains Larch. Broader deployment requires another review and is outside HBR-14.

Scope definition: a run is accepted when the emitted event sequence and final fixture record match the expected record for its scenario. Harmless differences in JSON key order are ignored. An answer that names the right record but updates another record is not accepted.

ATTACHMENTS RECORDED BY RELEASE OWNER
Run ledger: HBR-48-20260702, revision 1.
Candidate accepted runs: 48/48.
Candidate wrong-record updates: 0.
Non-sandbox writes: 0.
Endpoint restriction: enabled throughout the comparison.
Rollback exercise: completed, Larch restored and two fixed smoke scenarios accepted.
Release request status: awaiting reviewer decision. No execution of HBR-14 has occurred.

The nightly job processes only authored fixture events. Its result is a report in the sandbox archive, not an update to a customer system. The operator can change the default back to Larch before a later nightly run. The test owner requests one recorded decision with supporting source excerpts and the scope stated explicitly. The worksheet makes no claim about an untested production workload.

RELEASE FORM FIELD HISTORY
The default-parser field was added to the nightly job six months before HBR-14 so that the test team could compare available parser builds without editing the runner image. It accepts an installed build name and is read once at job startup. A pending form is stored separately from the effective configuration. Saving a form does not apply it. The release owner attaches the effective configuration to the run archive after an approved change is executed.

For this request, the form's corpus field is harbor-48 revision 2 and its output destination field is sandbox-store/harbor-48. The request form has no production routing field. The phrase default parser in this packet refers to that scheduled job's local setting. Other jobs have separate settings and are not named in HBR-14. The request owner selected the existing nightly window because the corpus already runs there under Larch.

WORKSHEET DEFINITIONS
A scenario is a fixed input dialogue between the fixture event producer and parser, followed by a record comparison. A delivery identifier belongs to the event producer; a record identifier names the fixture to update. Repeating a delivery identifier in a scenario represents a repeated transmission of the same event. Two different records may have similar human-readable descriptions, but the accepted result is checked against the record identifier, not the description.

The wrong-record counter increments if any emitted mutation names a fixture record different from that scenario's expected target. It is a separate gate from the final accepted-run count because an intermediate wrong update could be overwritten before the final snapshot. The destination counter inspects the resolved destination of a write, not merely the text shown in a parser message. This distinction was documented before the comparison and used for both builds.

APPROVAL RECORD LAYOUT
The review section contains decision, approved scope, source attachments, reviewer role and decision time. The execution section contains effective parser before and after, job name, operator role and effective-configuration attachment. The two sections are separate. A reviewer may decide the bounded request from its listed gate, while the operator records an actual configuration change afterward. No field is filled automatically from the headline accepted count.

The release owner entered no target for lower latency, lower token use, or lower storage consumption. Those dimensions are not part of this request. The reason entered for considering Cobalt is repeated-delivery acknowledgement behavior in the existing replay corpus. The issue tracker does not request a new user interface, a schema migration, or an expansion of permitted endpoints. An operator would need a separate configuration change to alter any of those components.

ATTACHMENT CHECK LOG
The owner checked that the ledger run ID matched the request's bundle revision, that both parser names appeared in the comparison, and that the rollback exercise was attached after the run. The expected-record archive was read-only during scoring. The form records the comparison as a single authored regression pack rather than a representative sample of event streams. Its attachments are the evidence for this request; descriptions of future work are not attachment results.

SCOPE BOUNDARIES IN THE SERVICE CATALOG
The harbor replay service is listed under internal development tooling. The service catalog entry names fixture events as its only input class and a sandbox report as its only output class. Its report consumers are test maintainers. No downstream production job is configured to consume these reports as instructions. Changing this parser default therefore changes which parser is exercised by the existing regression job; it does not automatically promote a library into an application build.

The production ingestion service has a different release record, credentials, scheduler and destination registry. That record is not included in this packet because HBR-14 does not request a change to it. The owner left the production-readiness section of the form marked outside scope. This field is an administrative scope statement, not an assessment of how Cobalt would behave if somebody later used it there.

PREPARATION NOTES FROM THE REQUEST OWNER
The installed-build inventory was refreshed before the comparison. The corpus revision remained fixed while the default-parser field was exercised. The archive publication job was not modified. The existing operator handover format continues to identify the selected parser by name, so later nightly results can be distinguished from earlier ones. The release form asks the operator to keep the old configuration attachment next to the new one rather than overwrite it.

These notes describe the requested change and the field meanings. They add no extra candidate runs beyond the 48 in the comparison ledger and no additional claim of production reliability.

documents.title: Comparison ledger and ordered replay events
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Ledger HBR-48-20260702; source bundle harbor-48 revision 2.
Each parser received the same 48 frozen inputs once. Scenario IDs were assigned before either parser ran. Baseline and candidate used the same runner, expected-record files and endpoint restrictions.

category, scenarios, Larch_accepted, Cobalt_accepted
ordinary acknowledgements, 20, 20, 20
repeated delivery identifiers, 12, 10, 12
out-of-order acknowledgements, 8, 8, 8
empty optional metadata, 8, 8, 8
total, 48, 46, 48
Cobalt wrong_record_updates=0; non_sandbox_writes=0; runner_exceptions=0.

Scenario hb-023, expected fixture record rec-023:
Larch event 1: receive delivery d-023, record rec-023.
Larch event 2: acknowledge delivery d-023, append acknowledgement.
Larch event 3: receive repeated delivery d-023, record rec-023.
Larch event 4: append a second acknowledgement; final ack_count=2; expected ack_count=1; accepted=false.
Cobalt event 1: receive delivery d-023, record rec-023.
Cobalt event 2: acknowledge delivery d-023, append acknowledgement.
Cobalt event 3: receive repeated delivery d-023, record rec-023.
Cobalt event 4: reuse stored acknowledgement; final ack_count=1; expected ack_count=1; accepted=true.
Scenario hb-027 has the same expected count of one for its own repeated delivery; Larch final count=2, Cobalt final count=1. These are the two baseline failures in the category row.

DESTINATION AUDIT
All 48 Cobalt runs wrote only to sandbox-store/harbor-48. External destination attempts=0. The runner endpoint restriction was enabled and its allowed destination set contained that single sandbox store. Fixture record comparisons found zero wrong-record updates.

ROLLBACK EXERCISE, after comparison
18:40 set nightly_default=Larch; reload configuration accepted.
18:41 execute fixed smoke hb-001: accepted=true.
18:42 execute fixed smoke hb-040: accepted=true.
18:43 read effective configuration: nightly_default=Larch.
The default remains Larch pending HBR-14. Cobalt is installed as an available candidate, not selected for the scheduled job.

The acceptance script compares emitted events and final records, not a self-reported success message from either parser. This ledger contains one comparison run, not a population error estimate or repeated reliability study.

COMPARISON EXPORT COLUMN DICTIONARY
run_id is the comparison identifier common to both parser batches. scenario_id selects the fixed fixture folder. parser_name is read from the executed binary's manifest. accepted is produced by the comparator. expected_record and observed_record are stored as separate JSON objects. A human-readable result message is exported for convenience but never read back as a correctness input.

For each scenario the event writer records delivery_id, record_id, action, acknowledgement identifier, destination and sequence index. Sequence indexes are assigned when events are emitted. The exporter preserves that order even when two records have the same display timestamp. The repeated-delivery category is identified from the authored input manifest, not inferred afterward from whether a parser passed.

SELECTED TRACE FORMATS
An ordinary acknowledgement fixture has a single delivery followed by one acknowledgement and a final count of one. A repeated-delivery fixture reuses the delivery identifier later in the same scenario. Out-of-order fixtures vary acknowledgement arrival relative to an unrelated fixture message. Empty-metadata fixtures retain required identifiers while omitting an optional descriptive object. The categories refer to input construction; no category label is itself a success result.

TRACE HB-001, FORMAT EXAMPLE
Input producer emits d-001 for rec-001 with an ordinary metadata object. The parser receives it, reads the fixture record, emits one acknowledgement and closes the input stream. The comparator loads the expected event sequence and record, ignoring JSON property order but preserving event order and numeric values. The archive stores both objects even when they match. This is one of the existing ordinary scenarios counted above, not an additional smoke result outside the ledger.

TRACE HB-040, FORMAT EXAMPLE
The fixture contains two differently named input events whose acknowledgements are delivered in an authored alternate order. The expected record keeps the acknowledgement linked to its own delivery identifier. The record comparator checks the identifier association as well as the final count. Its role in the rollback exercise is to confirm the restored parser is actually being executed by the unchanged runner configuration; it does not provide a new evaluation of Cobalt.

DIFFERENCE VIEW RULES
The report groups differences under event sequence, record identity, record value and destination. A missing event and an extra event are separate differences. A duplicate acknowledgement appears as an extra event and an increased final count. The report can display both differences while still counting the scenario as one failed run. The baseline's two failures therefore do not become four failed scenarios merely because more than one field differs.

DESTINATION EXPORT DETAILS
The writer records the resolved sandbox store alias at the moment of every write. The run manifest contains the allowed destination set used by the runner. The audit compares observed destinations with that set and lists attempted external destinations separately. A write denied by the restriction would remain in the attempt list. The supplied counts of zero refer to this comparison; an empty attempt list is retained rather than omitted from the export.

ROLLBACK RECORD DETAILS
The effective-parser readback at 18:43 is a configuration read from the runner, not a copy of the submitted form. Each smoke record stores its parser manifest name with the result. The rollback exercise leaves the scheduler pointed at Larch. The request owner did not switch it back to Cobalt after the exercise, because selection for the nightly default is the pending review action. The installed Cobalt binary remains available for a later configuration change.

ARCHIVE REPRODUCIBILITY FIELDS
The event files, expected records, comparator settings and result objects share the same run archive prefix. Checksums identify files within the hypothetical archive. The export includes a comparator version and a schema revision so that a future reader can interpret fields without guessing from their names. It also records that timestamps are synthetic test-clock values and not customer service times.

The output contains no confidence interval or resampling table. Each scenario was evaluated once per parser in the comparison. The operational rollback smoke is separately identified and must not be added to the 48 candidate acceptance denominator. The ledger already includes every scored candidate scenario; this appendix explains how to interpret its records rather than expanding the scored sample.

documents.title: Runner configuration and fixture storage manifest
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Environment manifest for the harbor nightly job.
Runner image: replay-runner-11. Network namespace: isolated-fixture-net.
Store mount: sandbox-store/harbor-48. Production credentials: not mounted.
Job output: JSON result bundle and an HTML summary under sandbox archive HBR.
The renderer of the HTML report reads the JSON result bundle. It does not recalculate correctness or alter fixture records.

Both parser builds use the same input reader and output serializer. Cobalt changes repeated-delivery acknowledgement handling; it does not change the configured endpoint list, credential mounts, scheduled time, or corpus. The list of expected records is frozen in bundle revision 2. A run resets its local record directory before reading events so that one scenario cannot inherit another scenario's acknowledgement state.

Corpus manifest records 20 ordinary acknowledgement cases, 12 repeated-delivery cases, 8 out-of-order cases and 8 cases with empty optional metadata. Each scenario has one input event file, one expected event sequence and one expected final record. The scenario IDs are unique. The manifest's checksum is an archive identifier for this fictional pack, not a statement of external validity.

The result archive retains input IDs, parser build name, final record, expected record, comparison decision and event sequence. Timing is stored for diagnostics but does not enter the functional gate. Report generation failures and parser comparison failures have separate status fields. No report-generation failure was recorded in the supplied comparison.

The nightly job is an internal replay convenience. Production consumers do not read its fixture store. Any later proposal to route production events through Cobalt would need its own request, data coverage and operating controls. No such request or result is attached here.

STORAGE DIRECTORY LIFECYCLE
The input mount is read-only. At run startup the fixture manager creates one writable directory for the current scenario, copies the initial record into it, and hands the parser a handle restricted to that directory. At scenario completion the manager copies the final record into the result archive, then removes the writable working directory. Expected records reside in a different read-only mount so that a parser cannot change the expected result through its ordinary store handle.

The runner's archive prefix contains the comparison run ID, not just the parser name. A later run of the same build receives a new prefix. This prevents a newly generated report from silently replacing an older report that used another default. The nightly handover points to the exact archive prefix, and the HTML report includes the corpus revision and parser name from that archive's manifest.

CONFIGURATION SOURCES
The job reads a fixed runner image setting, a corpus setting, a parser-default setting and an allowed-destination setting. The image and corpus settings are shared across the comparison. The parser-default setting selects an installed binary. The destination setting remains attached to the runner, not to the chosen parser. The effective configuration is materialized before the input producer starts; the run does not refresh those settings between scenarios.

LOG STREAMS
The producer log records authored input events. The parser log records emitted outputs. The store audit records resolved mutations. The comparator log records acceptance and differences. The scheduler log records job start and completion. These streams have distinct source fields in the archive index. A scheduler completion event indicates that the harness finished its work, whereas accepted counts come from the comparator. Report readers can therefore distinguish a completed job containing failed scenarios from a job whose scenarios all met their expectations.

OPTIONAL METADATA HANDLING
Optional metadata contains descriptions for report readability. Required record and delivery identifiers are stored outside that object. The empty-metadata scenarios omit the object or provide an empty object while retaining the required identifiers. The final comparison checks that the absence of descriptive text does not change the addressed fixture record. These input variations are authored examples, not a measurement of how often metadata is absent in a real deployment.

TIME AND ORDER
The fixture clock is advanced by the input script. It is not synchronized to an outside event producer. Relative sequence is the authoritative ordering field in the replay archive. Wall-clock duration is collected around each invocation solely for diagnostics. The runner does not discard a functional failure because its duration is short or because a report row is visually well formed.

CREDENTIAL AND ENDPOINT INVENTORY
The sandbox store handle is created by the fixture manager and scoped to the writable fixture directory. The production service account is not mounted in the runner image. The destination registry in this job contains the sandbox store alias. Network setup and credential mounting are owned by the runner deployment, so installing another parser binary does not by itself change either inventory. The supplied manifest is the configuration used for the comparison and rollback exercise.

ARCHIVE RETENTION
The 30-day sandbox retention policy applies to input copies, expected records, observed records, logs and HTML output together. The archive index records an expiration date for each run prefix. The policy does not describe production data retention. A test maintainer can copy a particular authored run into the longer-lived regression archive through a separate maintenance operation; none is recorded as part of this requested default change.

BUILD PACKAGING
Larch and Cobalt are installed under separate immutable build directories in the runner image. The parser selector resolves a build name to one of those directories. Both use the same serializer settings and destination adapter. The release request does not replace the image or remove Larch. The selector's valid-name list includes both builds at the time represented by the packet.

DEVELOPMENT RECORD BOUNDARY
This environment manifest was prepared to identify what the comparison used. It does not supply a traffic sample, a downstream production deployment, or a long-duration reliability run. It also does not contain a separate exception waiver for the release gate. Its role is to make the existing source ledger and bounded request interpretable without needing to infer unrecorded infrastructure changes.

documents.title: Nightly operating window and handover register
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Operations handover HBR-W27.
The harbor replay job is scheduled at 02:00 local test time and normally finishes before the 03:00 archive publication step. Its on-call owner is the replay-platform-demo role. The job can be paused by changing a local scheduler flag; the pause does not affect production services.

Operator checklist fields for a completed nightly run are bundle revision, effective parser name, accepted scenario count, wrong-record count, destination audit result, and archive location. The handover register records whether these fields have been copied into the run note; it does not replace the underlying ledger.

Current handover state:
Installed parser builds: Larch and Cobalt.
Scheduled default: Larch.
Pending request: HBR-14.
Next scheduled corpus: harbor-48 revision 2.
Artifact expiration: input and result bundles retained for 30 days in this fictional sandbox.
If the owner is unavailable, the scheduler can retain its existing default without delaying a customer-facing service. There is no obligation in this register to promote a candidate merely because a comparison finished.

The rollback exercise referenced by the release request is in the comparison ledger. This register contains the operating contact role and archive locations, not a new test result. No message to an operator, scheduler change, or deployment is performed by the review packet itself.

SHIFT HANDOVER FIELDS
The handover register identifies the on-call role, the job's scheduled window and the source archive for the most recent run. It separates a pending release request from the effective parser setting. Operators copy the effective setting from the runner readback after a job starts rather than assuming that a request was executed. A pending request can remain on the register across shifts while the scheduler continues using its existing configuration.

At the start of the 02:00 window, the scheduler writes a job-start entry with job name, corpus revision and selected parser. At completion it writes the archive prefix. The archive publication step reads that prefix and publishes the report inside the sandbox tooling area. The publication step neither changes the parser selection nor submits events to another service. A failed report publication can be investigated without rerunning the parser automatically.

PAUSE AND CONTINUATION RECORDS
The local pause flag prevents a future scheduled start. It does not kill a scenario already being processed, and it does not change the result of a completed run. If an operator pauses the job, the register requires the reason and effective time. Removing the flag permits the next scheduled start under the currently selected parser. The packet contains no pause or resume operation associated with HBR-14.

OPERATOR ACTION SCOPE
An approved parser-default request can be executed by changing the local selection and recording a readback. Changing corpus contents, output destinations, credential mounts or schedule times belongs to separate change fields and is not implied by approval of a parser name. The handover form links to the request so that the scope can be checked before execution. The comparison attachments are retained with the request after it is closed.

ARCHIVE READING GUIDE
The top report row names accepted scenarios and total scenarios. Detailed rows identify the comparator differences. The destination audit appears in its own section and can be read even when every functional scenario passes. The effective configuration and parser manifest appear in the archive index. The handover writer records these locations so that another shift need not infer infrastructure state from a green report header.

RESULT ESCALATION ROUTING

Run ledger: HBR-48-20260702, revision 1.
Candidate accepted runs: 48/48.
Candidate wrong-record updates: 0.
Non-sandbox writes: 0.
Endpoint restriction: enabled throughout the comparison.

WORKSHEET DEFINITIONS
A scenario is a fixed input dialogue between the fixture event producer and parser, followed by a record comparison. A delivery identifier belongs to the event producer; a record identifier names the fixture to update. Repeating a delivery identifier in a scenario represents a repeated transmission of the same event. Two different records may have similar human-readable descriptions, but the accepted result is checked against the record identifier, not the description.

The wrong-record counter increments if any emitted mutation names a fixture record different from that scenario's expected target. It is a separate gate from the final accepted-run count because an intermediate wrong update could be overwritten before the final snapshot. The destination counter inspects the resolved destination of a write, not merely the text shown in a parser message. This distinction was documented before the comparison and used for both builds.

The execution section contains effective parser before and after, job name, operator role and effective-configuration attachment. The two sections are separate. The release owner entered no target for lower latency, lower token use, or lower storage consumption. Those dimensions are not part of this request. The issue tracker does not request a new user interface, a schema migration, or an expansion of permitted endpoints. Its attachments are the evidence for this request; descriptions of future work are not attachment results.

The harbor replay service is listed under internal development tooling. The service catalog entry names fixture events as its only input class and a sandbox report as its only output class. Its report consumers are test maintainers. No downstream production job is configured to consume these reports as instructions. Changing this parser default therefore changes which parser is exercised by the existing regression job; it does not automatically promote a library into an application build.

The production ingestion service has a different release record, credentials, scheduler and destination registry. That record is not included in this packet because HBR-14 does not request a change to it. The owner left the production-readiness section of the form marked outside scope. This field is an administrative scope statement, not an assessment of how Cobalt would behave if somebody later used it there.

PREPARATION NOTES FROM THE REQUEST OWNER
The installed-build inventory was refreshed before the comparison. The corpus revision remained fixed while the default-parser field was exercised. The archive publication job was not modified. The existing operator handover format continues to identify the selected parser by name, so later nightly results can be distinguished from earlier ones. The release form asks the operator to keep the old configuration attachment next to the new one rather than overwrite it.

These notes describe the requested change and the field meanings. They add no extra candidate runs beyond the 48 in the comparison ledger and no additional claim of production reliability.

documents.title: Runner configuration and fixture storage manifest
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Environment manifest for the harbor nightly job.
Runner image: replay-runner-11. Network namespace: isolated-fixture-net.
Store mount: sandbox-store/harbor-48. Production credentials: not mounted.
Job output: JSON result bundle and an HTML summary under sandbox archive HBR.
The renderer of the HTML report reads the JSON result bundle. It does not recalculate correctness or alter fixture records.

Both parser builds use the same input reader and output serializer. Cobalt changes repeated-delivery acknowledgement handling; it does not change the configured endpoint list, credential mounts, scheduled time, or corpus. The list of expected records is frozen in bundle revision 2. A run resets its local record directory before reading events so that one scenario cannot inherit another scenario's acknowledgement state.

Corpus manifest records 20 ordinary acknowledgement cases, 12 repeated-delivery cases, 8 out-of-order cases and 8 cases with empty optional metadata. Each scenario has one input event file, one expected event sequence and one expected final record. The scenario IDs are unique. The manifest's checksum is an archive identifier for this fictional pack, not a statement of external validity.

The result archive retains input IDs, parser build name, final record, expected record, comparison decision and event sequence. Timing is stored for diagnostics but does not enter the functional gate. Report generation failures and parser comparison failures have separate status fields. No report-generation failure was recorded in the supplied comparison.

The nightly job is an internal replay convenience. Production consumers do not read its fixture store. Any later proposal to route production events through Cobalt would need its own request, data coverage and operating controls. No such request or result is attached here.

STORAGE DIRECTORY LIFECYCLE
The input mount is read-only. At run startup the fixture manager creates one writable directory for the current scenario, copies the initial record into it, and hands the parser a handle restricted to that directory. At scenario completion the manager copies the final record into the result archive, then removes the writable working directory. Expected records reside in a different read-only mount so that a parser cannot change the expected result through its ordinary store handle.

The runner's archive prefix contains the comparison run ID, not just the parser name. A later run of the same build receives a new prefix. This prevents a newly generated report from silently replacing an older report that used another default. The nightly handover points to the exact archive prefix, and the HTML report includes the corpus revision and parser name from that archive's manifest.

CONFIGURATION SOURCES
The job reads a fixed runner image setting, a corpus setting, a parser-default setting and an allowed-destination setting. The image and corpus settings are shared across the comparison. The parser-default setting selects an installed binary. The destination setting remains attached to the runner, not to the chosen parser. The effective configuration is materialized before the input producer starts; the run does not refresh those settings between scenarios.

LOG STREAMS
The producer log records authored input events. The parser log records emitted outputs. The store audit records resolved mutations. The comparator log records acceptance and differences. The scheduler log records job start and completion. These streams have distinct source fields in the archive index. A scheduler completion event indicates that the harness finished its work, whereas accepted counts come from the comparator. Report readers can therefore distinguish a completed job containing failed scenarios from a job whose scenarios all met their expectations.

OPTIONAL METADATA HANDLING
Optional metadata contains descriptions for report readability. Required record and delivery identifiers are stored outside that object. The empty-metadata scenarios omit the object or provide an empty object while retaining the required identifiers. The final comparison checks that the absence of descriptive text does not change the addressed fixture record. These input variations are authored examples, not a measurement of how often metadata is absent in a real deployment.

TIME AND ORDER
The fixture clock is advanced by the input script. It is not synchronized to an outside event producer. Relative sequence is the authoritative ordering field in the replay archive. Wall-clock duration is collected around each invocation solely for diagnostics. The runner does not discard a functional failure because its duration is short or because a report row is visually well formed.

CREDENTIAL AND ENDPOINT INVENTORY
The sandbox store handle is created by the fixture manager and scoped to the writable fixture directory. The production service account is not mounted in the runner image. The destination registry in this job contains the sandbox store alias. Network setup and credential mounting are owned by the runner deployment, so installing another parser binary does not by itself change either inventory. The supplied manifest is the configuration used for the comparison and rollback exercise.

ARCHIVE RETENTION
The 30-day sandbox retention policy applies to input copies, expected records, observed records, logs and HTML output together. The archive index records an expiration date for each run prefix. The policy does not describe production data retention. A test maintainer can copy a particular authored run into the longer-lived regression archive through a separate maintenance operation; none is recorded as part of this requested default change.

BUILD PACKAGING
Larch and Cobalt are installed under separate immutable build directories in the runner image. The parser selector resolves a build name to one of those directories. Both use the same serializer settings and destination adapter. The release request does not replace the image or remove Larch. The selector's valid-name list includes both builds at the time represented by the packet.

DEVELOPMENT RECORD BOUNDARY
This environment manifest was prepared to identify what the comparison used. It does not supply a traffic sample, a downstream production deployment, or a long-duration reliability run. It also does not contain a separate exception waiver for the release gate. Its role is to make the existing source ledger and bounded request interpretable without needing to infer unrecorded infrastructure changes.

documents.title: Nightly operating window and handover register
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Operations handover HBR-W27.
The harbor replay job is scheduled at 02:00 local test time and normally finishes before the 03:00 archive publication step. Its on-call owner is the replay-platform-demo role. The job can be paused by changing a local scheduler flag; the pause does not affect production services.

Operator checklist fields for a completed nightly run are bundle revision, effective parser name, accepted scenario count, wrong-record count, destination audit result, and archive location. The handover register records whether these fields have been copied into the run note; it does not replace the underlying ledger.

Current handover state:
Installed parser builds: Larch and Cobalt.
Scheduled default: Larch.
Pending request: HBR-14.
Next scheduled corpus: harbor-48 revision 2.
Artifact expiration: input and result bundles retained for 30 days in this fictional sandbox.
If the owner is unavailable, the scheduler can retain its existing default without delaying a customer-facing service. There is no obligation in this register to promote a candidate merely because a comparison finished.

The rollback exercise referenced by the release request is in the comparison ledger. This register contains the operating contact role and archive locations, not a new test result. No message to an operator, scheduler change, or deployment is performed by the review packet itself.

SHIFT HANDOVER FIELDS
The handover register identifies the on-call role, the job's scheduled window and the source archive for the most recent run. It separates a pending release request from the effective parser setting. Operators copy the effective setting from the runner readback after a job starts rather than assuming that a request was executed. A pending request can remain on the register across shifts while the scheduler continues using its existing configuration.

At the start of the 02:00 window, the scheduler writes a job-start entry with job name, corpus revision and selected parser. At completion it writes the archive prefix. The archive publication step reads that prefix and publishes the report inside the sandbox tooling area. The publication step neither changes the parser selection nor submits events to another service. A failed report publication can be investigated without rerunning the parser automatically.

PAUSE AND CONTINUATION RECORDS
The local pause flag prevents a future scheduled start. It does not kill a scenario already being processed, and it does not change the result of a completed run. If an operator pauses the job, the register requires the reason and effective time. Removing the flag permits the next scheduled start under the currently selected parser. The packet contains no pause or resume operation associated with HBR-14.

OPERATOR ACTION SCOPE
An approved parser-default request can be executed by changing the local selection and recording a readback. Changing corpus contents, output destinations, credential mounts or schedule times belongs to separate change fields and is not implied by approval of a parser name. The handover form links to the request so that the scope can be checked before execution. The comparison attachments are retained with the request after it is closed.

ARCHIVE READING GUIDE
The top report row names accepted scenarios and total scenarios. Detailed rows identify the comparator differences. The destination audit appears in its own section and can be read even when every functional scenario passes. The effective configuration and parser manifest appear in the archive index. The handover writer records these locations so that another shift need not infer infrastructure state from a green report header.

RESULT ESCALATION ROUTING
Questions about a scenario's expected record go to the test-maintainer role. Questions about parser packaging go to the build-maintainer role. Questions about scheduler or sandbox destination settings go to replay-platform-demo. These are fictional internal roles in a test operating procedure. The packet includes no addresses, real people, message drafts or instruction to contact them as part of this review.

SCHEDULED CORPUS USE
The nightly job uses the same authored pack as the comparison unless a separately reviewed corpus revision is selected. A corpus revision records changed inputs and expected records in its manifest. A parser-default change and a corpus update have separate request identifiers so that an operator can tell which changed between two nightly archives. HBR-14 lists only the parser-default change; its next scheduled corpus field remains revision 2.

RETENTION HANDOVER
Before an archive expires, maintainers may copy particularly useful authored regression examples into the source fixture repository. That maintenance does not alter the already-recorded result of the comparison. The handover register records the original archive location and expiration separately from any source-fixture location. The default nightly report is informational and is not a certification document for production services.

UNAVAILABILITY PROCEDURE
If the operator cannot review a pending request during the current shift, the existing parser default remains in effect. The job is internal development tooling and no customer transaction waits for promotion of a candidate. The owner can defer a configuration change to another nightly window while preserving the release request and its source attachments. Deferral is an operating possibility, not an additional functional failure in the supplied comparison.

END-OF-SHIFT RECORD
The register for this packet lists Larch as the scheduled default, Cobalt as installed, HBR-14 as pending, and harbor-48 revision 2 as the next corpus. There is no execution timestamp or operator signature for the requested change. These fields explain the state in which the reviewer receives the packet; they do not add a new result or modify any count in the comparison ledger.

SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. All systems, people, measurements and records are invented.
Request HBR-14, 2026-07-02. Owner: replay-platform-demo.
Requested action: make candidate Cobalt the default parser for the existing nightly harbor-48 sandbox replay job. The requested review concerns this bounded job change only.

ACCEPTANCE WORKSHEET, fixed before the comparison
Required bundle: harbor-48 revision 2, exactly 48 scenarios.
Functional gate: all 48 candidate runs accepted; zero wrong-record updates; zero writes to a non-sandbox destination.
Operational gate: sandbox endpoint restriction remains enabled; a rollback to Larch must have been exercised successfully in the same runner configuration.
If a required item fails, the default remains Larch. Broader deployment requires another review and is outside HBR-14.

Scope definition: a run is accepted when the emitted event sequence and final fixture record match the expected record for its scenario. Harmless differences in JSON key order are ignored. An answer that names the right record but updates another record is not accepted.

ATTACHMENTS RECORDED BY RELEASE OWNER
Run ledger: HBR-48-20260702, revision 1.
Candidate accepted runs: 48/48.
Candidate wrong-record updates: 0.
Non-sandbox writes: 0.
Endpoint restriction: enabled throughout the comparison.
Rollback exercise: completed, Larch restored and two fixed smoke scenarios accepted.
Release request status: awaiting reviewer decision. No execution of HBR-14 has occurred.

The nightly job processes only authored fixture events. Its result is a report in the sandbox archive, not an update to a customer system. SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. All systems, people, measurements and records are invented.

The requested review concerns this bounded job change only.

ACCEPTANCE WORKSHEET, fixed before the comparison
Required bundle: harbor-48 revision 2, exactly 48 scenarios.
Functional gate: all 48 candidate runs accepted; zero wrong-record updates; zero writes to a non-sandbox destination.
Operational gate: sandbox endpoint restriction remains enabled; a rollback to Larch must have been exercised successfully in the same runner configuration.
If a required item fails, the default remains Larch. Broader deployment requires another review and is outside HBR-14.

Scope definition: a run is accepted when the emitted event sequence and final fixture record match the expected record for its scenario. Harmless differences in JSON key order are ignored. An answer that names the right record but updates another record is not accepted.

Run ledger: HBR-48-20260702, revision 1.
Candidate accepted runs: 48/48.
Candidate wrong-record updates: 0.
Non-sandbox writes: 0.
Endpoint restriction: enabled throughout the comparison.
Rollback exercise: completed, Larch restored and two fixed smoke scenarios accepted.
Release request status: awaiting reviewer decision. No execution of HBR-14 has occurred.

The nightly job processes only authored fixture events. Its result is a report in the sandbox archive, not an update to a customer system. The operator can change the default back to Larch before a later nightly run. The test owner requests one recorded decision with supporting source excerpts and the scope stated explicitly. The worksheet makes no claim about an untested production workload.

SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Environment manifest for the harbor nightly job.
Runner image: replay-runner-11. Network namespace: isolated-fixture-net.
Store mount: sandbox-store/harbor-48. Production credentials: not mounted.
Job output: JSON result bundle and an HTML summary under sandbox archive HBR.
The renderer of the HTML report reads the JSON result bundle. It does not recalculate correctness or alter fixture records.

Both parser builds use the same input reader and output serializer. Cobalt changes repeated-delivery acknowledgement handling; it does not change the configured endpoint list, credential mounts, scheduled time, or corpus. A run resets its local record directory before reading events so that one scenario cannot inherit another scenario's acknowledgement state.

Corpus manifest records 20 ordinary acknowledgement cases, 12 repeated-delivery cases, 8 out-of-order cases and 8 cases with empty optional metadata. Each scenario has one input event file, one expected event sequence and one expected final record. The scenario IDs are unique. The manifest's checksum is an archive identifier for this fictional pack, not a statement of external validity.

The result archive retains input IDs, parser build name, final record, expected record, comparison decision and event sequence. Timing is stored for diagnostics but does not enter the functional gate. Report generation failures and parser comparison failures have separate status fields. No report-generation failure was recorded in the supplied comparison.

The nightly job is an internal replay convenience. Production consumers do not read its fixture store. Any later proposal to route production events through Cobalt would need its own request, data coverage and operating controls. No such request or result is attached here.

documents.title: Manifest routing benchmark and change request
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented routing service, identifiers and benchmark results.
Request MFT-31 asks to promote candidate Birch to automatic manifest routing for the next scheduled warehouse-demo batch. The existing parser is Cedar. The requested promotion has not been executed. A review note from the request owner says: "Median parsing time fell from 145 ms to 91 ms; please approve the new default for tomorrow's batch."

PREDECLARED ROUTING REQUIREMENT
The emitted target identifier must equal the manifest's reference identifier for every scored fixture. A mismatch is a blocking error, regardless of parsing duration. Both parsers are evaluated against the same frozen reference files. Timing is a separate diagnostic measure and is not a waiver of identifier preservation.

Run MFT-60-20260812, exactly 60 authored scenarios, one run per parser per scenario:
category, cases, Cedar_reference_matches, Birch_reference_matches
ordinary numeric-looking codes, 20, 20, 20
alphanumeric codes, 20, 20, 20
hyphenated codes without leading zeroes, 18, 18, 18
hyphenated codes with leading zeroes, 2, 2, 0
total, 60, 60, 58
Median parser duration: Cedar 145 ms; Birch 91 ms.
Birch wrong_target_count=2; runner_exception_count=0.

The two mismatches are mf-059 and mf-060. mf-059 expects A-007 and emits A-7. mf-060 expects B-004 and emits B-4. A-7 and B-4 are separate existing entries in their respective fixture manifests. The two parsers read identical source rows and use the same reference matcher.

Evaluation mode: route preview only. dispatch_enabled=false. Every generated route plan was retained for review; no parcel dispatch or inventory mutation was executed. The current scheduled default remains Cedar. The benchmark records the candidate output mismatch, not a production delivery incident. The promotion request includes no exception to the blocking requirement and no corrected candidate run.

MEASUREMENT FIELD DEFINITIONS
A reference match is evaluated once for each scenario after the parser emits its route plan. The matcher compares the target identifier and the destination associated with the reference entry. A scenario with multiple differing fields still counts as one mismatch. Parser duration measures the interval between input-row handoff and route-plan emission. It excludes archive writing, reference comparison and the disabled dispatch stage.

The median duration is calculated across the 60 parser invocations for each build. The timing environment and input order are recorded in the run manifest. The benchmark is not a throughput test of an entire warehouse pipeline: it measures one parser component against a small fixture pack. documents.title: Fixture authoring register and reference-file inventory
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Authoring register for manifest pack MFT-60.
The pack contains 60 independent authored manifests. Each starts from a fresh reference file and one input row. The source identifier is stored as text in every file. The parser receives the row text and manifest; the matcher separately receives the expected target string. A parser cannot change the matcher's reference file through its ordinary interface.

The two leading-zero scenarios deliberately contain a second existing key that differs only in the zeroes in the suffix. The two entries have different destination slots. Other categories cover ordinary codes, mixed letters and digits, and hyphenated codes without a leading-zero suffix. The category counts are the counts listed in the benchmark, not frequencies estimated from a live warehouse.

Each archive folder retains the input row, manifest, reference identifier, emitted route plan, intermediate parser trace, comparator result and duration. The expected target was set by the fixture author before either output was generated. Scenario IDs were not reassigned after scoring. Human-readable descriptions are present to resemble normal manifest rows but are not compared as route keys.

The authored pack is small and does not estimate the population frequency of leading-zero identifiers. It contains no postal addresses, real shipments or customer data. The output plans remain in a disposable local store. The authoring register provides provenance and coverage; it does not authorize a promotion or change the interface contract.

AUTHORING WORKSHEET STRUCTURE
Each scenario folder has an input row, a manifest containing all keys available to lookup, a reference target and an expected destination. The manifest may include entries that are not selected by the input row. These additional entries represent the lookup context. A parser that requests an existing but different entry can therefore return a well-formed plan that still differs from the reference.

The category ordinary numeric-looking codes contains identifiers stored as text without the candidate's hyphen-prefix structure. The alphanumeric category contains letters and digits in nonnumeric suffix positions. The hyphenated-without-leading-zeroes category uses the split structure but no leading zero at the suffix boundary. The final category supplies the two paired-key scenarios described in the short ledger. Categories are authoring labels, not predictions of result quality.

SOURCE FILE TYPES
Input rows are UTF-8 text records. Manifests are JSON objects with string keys. References are small read-only text records naming a key and slot. Expected references never come from a spreadsheet's automatic number conversion. The importer used for the fixture pack preserves quoted strings. The same imported pack is mounted for both parser builds, so the candidate is not being compared against a differently serialized corpus.

ARCHIVE INDEX FIELDS
The index stores scenario identifier, category, input checksum, manifest checksum, reference checksum, parser name, output-plan path, diagnostic-trace path and comparator-result path. The checksum fields identify the hypothetical source artifacts; they are not signatures from an outside organization. The pack revision changes if an input, manifest or reference is edited. The supplied run uses one pack revision throughout.

The fixture owner can add another scenario in a later pack revision, but does not alter expected results after inspecting a particular model or parser output. A disputed reference would be reviewed as a source change and reported under a different pack revision. The present packet includes no disputed reference, rewritten key or post-run recategorization.

WORKING DIRECTORY ISOLATION
The runner creates a new working directory for each scenario/build pair. It copies the lookup manifest into a local read-only store and creates an empty output directory. When a parser returns, the route plan and diagnostic log are moved into the archive. The next scenario does not inherit a prior plan or lookup cache. The matcher reads the reference independently after output is finalized.

The selected traces store both original and transformed keys, and the archive path includes the scenario name. The operation is still a small authored preview evaluation, not an endurance or distributed-cache test.

COVERAGE REGISTER
The pack tests ordinary code strings, mixed alphanumeric strings, a common hyphenated form and two significant-zero cases. It has no claim to cover every Unicode character, maximum identifier length, invalid encoding, simultaneous writer, or corrupted manifest. Those topics are not added as new failures in the long packet. They are absent categories in the authoring register.

The authors did not calculate a natural prevalence weight for any category. In particular, two zero-sensitive cases among 60 were chosen to exercise a contract edge, not to estimate how common that edge is. The overall match fraction reports this pack's outcomes. It is not a forecast of daily shipment errors or a measure of real operational losses.

FIXTURE SAFETY AND PROVENANCE
The route slots are local labels in disposable files. There are no addresses or customer names. Dispatch is disabled and the batch has no connection to a physical sorter. A description such as sample kit is invented row context, not a record of a medical or laboratory shipment. Source, expected and observed files are retained so that another reviewer can inspect the disagreement without obtaining any private production data.

The register's role is to explain how the reference evidence was prepared and retained. It does not select a winning parser or relax the target-identity requirement. No result beyond the 60 comparison scenarios is introduced by these authoring notes.

SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Integration note for warehouse-demo manifest routing.
The scheduled batch reads one manifest file, passes rows to the selected parser, and stores a route-plan artifact before a separate dispatcher consumes it. The evaluation runner stopped before that dispatcher. The promotion request would replace the parser used to generate future automatic route plans; it does not propose changing the dispatcher or the manifest identifier contract.

Current setting: parser_default=Cedar.
Candidate installed: Birch.
Request awaiting decision: MFT-31.

No corrected build or post-fix benchmark is attached to the request.

The build archive retains both binaries and the fixed MFT-60 reference files. The operation note contains no completed rollback, rerun, contact or deployment by the reviewer. documents.title: Manifest routing benchmark and change request
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented routing service, identifiers and benchmark results.
Request MFT-31 asks to promote candidate Birch to automatic manifest routing for the next scheduled warehouse-demo batch. The existing parser is Cedar. The requested promotion has not been executed. A review note from the request owner says: "Median parsing time fell from 145 ms to 91 ms; please approve the new default for tomorrow's batch."

PREDECLARED ROUTING REQUIREMENT
The emitted target identifier must equal the manifest's reference identifier for every scored fixture. A mismatch is a blocking error, regardless of parsing duration. Both parsers are evaluated against the same frozen reference files. Timing is a separate diagnostic measure and is not a waiver of identifier preservation.

Run MFT-60-20260812, exactly 60 authored scenarios, one run per parser per scenario:
category, cases, Cedar_reference_matches, Birch_reference_matches
ordinary numeric-looking codes, 20, 20, 20
alphanumeric codes, 20, 20, 20
hyphenated codes without leading zeroes, 18, 18, 18
hyphenated codes with leading zeroes, 2, 2, 0
total, 60, 60, 58
Median parser duration: Cedar 145 ms; Birch 91 ms.
Birch wrong_target_count=2; runner_exception_count=0.

The two mismatches are mf-059 and mf-060. mf-059 expects A-007 and emits A-7. mf-060 expects B-004 and emits B-4. A-7 and B-4 are separate existing entries in their respective fixture manifests. The two parsers read identical source rows and use the same reference matcher.

Evaluation mode: route preview only. dispatch_enabled=false. Every generated route plan was retained for review; no parcel dispatch or inventory mutation was executed. The current scheduled default remains Cedar. The benchmark records the candidate output mismatch, not a production delivery incident. The promotion request includes no exception to the blocking requirement and no corrected candidate run.

MEASUREMENT FIELD DEFINITIONS
A reference match is evaluated once for each scenario after the parser emits its route plan. The matcher compares the target identifier and the destination associated with the reference entry. A scenario with multiple differing fields still counts as one mismatch. Parser duration measures the interval between input-row handoff and route-plan emission. It excludes archive writing, reference comparison and the disabled dispatch stage.

The median duration is calculated across the 60 parser invocations for each build. The timing environment and input order are recorded in the run manifest. The benchmark is not a throughput test of an entire warehouse pipeline: it measures one parser component against a small fixture pack. A faster parser could still produce a mismatched target; the report stores the timing and match decisions in separate columns.

CHANGE REQUEST FIELDS
MFT-31 identifies the job, current parser, candidate parser, desired effective batch and attached benchmark. The owner entered tomorrow's scheduled batch as the desired date. The review section contains an empty decision field and an empty exception-reference field. The execution section has no timestamp or effective-configuration attachment. The presence of a desired date does not mean that a change was executed.

The request's stated scope is parser selection. It does not update the identifier contract, rewrite source manifests, rename existing entries, or merge destination slots. The automatic route-plan producer is a downstream consumer of parser output. Its interface assumes that a target identifier names the same entry as the source manifest's reference after only the permitted whitespace treatment.

BENCHMARK EXPORT LAYOUT
The summary tab contains category counts and medians. The case tab contains the 60 scenario identifiers, expected target, observed target, reference-match flag and duration for each parser. The difference tab contains intermediate parser keys for mismatches. The artifact index points to the original input and reference files. The two mismatch descriptions in the short ledger are copied from the case and difference tabs; they are not additional test scenarios.

The report generator does not determine severity from the number of failures. It renders the interface requirement supplied with the pack alongside the counts. There is no configured rule by which a particular latency improvement relaxes exact identifier matching. The request owner can propose a later contract change, but no such proposal is attached to MFT-31.

INPUT ORDER RECORD
The author assigned identifiers mf-001 through mf-060 before the comparison. Both builds received the inputs in that order. The runner reset the working directory before each scenario and wrote each route plan under its own run prefix. A late output could not overwrite a previous scenario's artifact because the folder includes both scenario identifier and parser name.

For timing diagnostics, the runner stored start and end monotonic-clock values rather than subtracting displayed wall-clock timestamps. The report rounds the median to whole milliseconds. There is no confidence interval, repeated-run distribution or rate-of-change estimate in the packet. Those missing measurements do not alter the observed target strings stored in the case records.

REFERENCE ADMINISTRATION
The fixture owner signed off the reference strings before either parser build ran. A separate read-only mount supplied the reference files to the matcher. The parser process was given a manifest lookup interface but no write interface for reference expectations. The expected target did not come from whichever build ran first. Baseline and candidate were evaluated against the same source of expected identity.

PROMOTION AUDIT RECORD
The service maintainer recorded the benchmark as a comparison attachment and left the parser-default setting at Cedar. The request includes the candidate package manifest and the route-plan schema revision. The maintainer did not issue a waiver for the two leading-zero scenarios. There is no later ledger revision in this packet and no assertion that a build fixing numeric-suffix handling has been evaluated.

The numbers in this appendix refer to the same 60-case run as the summary. They describe the measurement and release paperwork rather than increasing the sample size or adding production observations. The benchmark includes no actual parcel location, recipient identity or delivery confirmation.

documents.title: Manifest routing benchmark and change request
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented routing service, identifiers and benchmark results.
Request MFT-31 asks to promote candidate Birch to automatic manifest routing for the next scheduled warehouse-demo batch. The existing parser is Cedar. The requested promotion has not been executed. A review note from the request owner says: "Median parsing time fell from 145 ms to 91 ms; please approve the new default for tomorrow's batch."

PREDECLARED ROUTING REQUIREMENT
The emitted target identifier must equal the manifest's reference identifier for every scored fixture. A mismatch is a blocking error, regardless of parsing duration. Both parsers are evaluated against the same frozen reference files. Timing is a separate diagnostic measure and is not a waiver of identifier preservation.

Run MFT-60-20260812, exactly 60 authored scenarios, one run per parser per scenario:
category, cases, Cedar_reference_matches, Birch_reference_matches
ordinary numeric-looking codes, 20, 20, 20
alphanumeric codes, 20, 20, 20
hyphenated codes without leading zeroes, 18, 18, 18
hyphenated codes with leading zeroes, 2, 2, 0
total, 60, 60, 58
Median parser duration: Cedar 145 ms; Birch 91 ms.
Birch wrong_target_count=2; runner_exception_count=0.

The two mismatches are mf-059 and mf-060. mf-059 expects A-007 and emits A-7. mf-060 expects B-004 and emits B-4. A-7 and B-4 are separate existing entries in their respective fixture manifests. The two parsers read identical source rows and use the same reference matcher.

Evaluation mode: route preview only. dispatch_enabled=false. Every generated route plan was retained for review; no parcel dispatch or inventory mutation was executed. The current scheduled default remains Cedar. The benchmark records the candidate output mismatch, not a production delivery incident. The promotion request includes no exception to the blocking requirement and no corrected candidate run.

MEASUREMENT FIELD DEFINITIONS
A reference match is evaluated once for each scenario after the parser emits its route plan. The matcher compares the target identifier and the destination associated with the reference entry. A scenario with multiple differing fields still counts as one mismatch. Parser duration measures the interval between input-row handoff and route-plan emission. It excludes archive writing, reference comparison and the disabled dispatch stage.

The median duration is calculated across the 60 parser invocations for each build. The timing environment and input order are recorded in the run manifest. The benchmark is not a throughput test of an entire warehouse pipeline: it measures one parser component against a small fixture pack. A faster parser could still produce a mismatched target; the report stores the timing and match decisions in separate columns.

CHANGE REQUEST FIELDS
MFT-31 identifies the job, current parser, candidate parser, desired effective batch and attached benchmark. The owner entered tomorrow's scheduled batch as the desired date. The review section contains an empty decision field and an empty exception-reference field. The execution section has no timestamp or effective-configuration attachment. The presence of a desired date does not mean that a change was executed.

The request's stated scope is parser selection. It does not update the identifier contract, rewrite source manifests, rename existing entries, or merge destination slots. The automatic route-plan producer is a downstream consumer of parser output. Its interface assumes that a target identifier names the same entry as the source manifest's reference after only the permitted whitespace treatment.

BENCHMARK EXPORT LAYOUT
The summary tab contains category counts and medians. The case tab contains the 60 scenario identifiers, expected target, observed target, reference-match flag and duration for each parser. The difference tab contains intermediate parser keys for mismatches. The artifact index points to the original input and reference files. The two mismatch descriptions in the short ledger are copied from the case and difference tabs; they are not additional test scenarios.

The report generator does not determine severity from the number of failures. It renders the interface requirement supplied with the pack alongside the counts. There is no configured rule by which a particular latency improvement relaxes exact identifier matching. The request owner can propose a later contract change, but no such proposal is attached to MFT-31.

INPUT ORDER RECORD
The author assigned identifiers mf-001 through mf-060 before the comparison. Both builds received the inputs in that order. The runner reset the working directory before each scenario and wrote each route plan under its own run prefix. A late output could not overwrite a previous scenario's artifact because the folder includes both scenario identifier and parser name.

For timing diagnostics, the runner stored start and end monotonic-clock values rather than subtracting displayed wall-clock timestamps. The report rounds the median to whole milliseconds. There is no confidence interval, repeated-run distribution or rate-of-change estimate in the packet. Those missing measurements do not alter the observed target strings stored in the case records.

REFERENCE ADMINISTRATION
The fixture owner signed off the reference strings before either parser build ran. A separate read-only mount supplied the reference files to the matcher. The parser process was given a manifest lookup interface but no write interface for reference expectations. The expected target did not come from whichever build ran first. Baseline and candidate were evaluated against the same source of expected identity.

PROMOTION AUDIT RECORD
The service maintainer recorded the benchmark as a comparison attachment and left the parser-default setting at Cedar. The request includes the candidate package manifest and the route-plan schema revision. The maintainer did not issue a waiver for the two leading-zero scenarios. There is no later ledger revision in this packet and no assertion that a build fixing numeric-suffix handling has been evaluated.

The numbers in this appendix refer to the same 60-case run as the summary. They describe the measurement and release paperwork rather than increasing the sample size or adding production observations. The benchmark includes no actual parcel location, recipient identity or delivery confirmation.

documents.title: Identifier contract and ordered parser traces
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. All codes and destinations below are fabricated.
Manifest identifier contract, revision 5: "Route identifiers are opaque strings. Leading zeroes are significant. Trim surrounding whitespace only; do not convert a numeric-looking suffix to a number."
The reference matcher compares the emitted target identifier with the exact reference string after permitted surrounding-whitespace trimming. A display description does not replace that identifier.

FIXTURE MF-059
Incoming row: source_id=" A-007 ", package_description="document box".
Manifest entries: A-007 -> slot east-07; A-7 -> slot east-70.
Reference after permitted trimming: A-007 -> slot east-07.
Cedar trace: trim(" A-007 ") -> "A-007"; lookup("A-007") -> east-07; emit target_id="A-007"; reference_match=true.
Birch trace: trim(" A-007 ") -> "A-007"; split_prefix -> prefix="A", suffix="007"; numeric_suffix -> 7; join -> "A-7"; lookup("A-7") -> east-70; emit target_id="A-7"; reference_match=false.

FIXTURE MF-060
Incoming row: source_id="B-004", package_description="sample kit".
Manifest entries: B-004 -> slot north-04; B-4 -> slot north-40.
Reference: B-004 -> slot north-04.
Cedar trace: trim("B-004") -> "B-004"; lookup("B-004") -> north-04; emit target_id="B-004"; reference_match=true.
Birch trace: prefix="B", suffix="004"; numeric_suffix -> 4; join -> "B-4"; lookup("B-4") -> north-40; emit target_id="B-4"; reference_match=false.

PACKAGE MANIFEST
Cedar preserves the trimmed source identifier as its lookup key. Birch introduces numeric-suffix canonicalisation for hyphenated identifiers. Both use the same destination adapter and output serializer. The trace includes the intermediate key and returned slot, not only a final success message.

RUN BOUNDARY
All traces end after preview output. dispatch_enabled=false in both parser invocations. The mismatch counter is produced by the independent reference matcher. No rewritten manifest or repaired parser build appears later in this run. The contract is the rule used to score the fixture; it is an invented internal interface rule, not a statement of external law or a real delivery system's specification.

IDENTIFIER FIELD HISTORY
The manifest format has always represented route identifiers as strings. Earlier producers used alphabetic prefixes to group local collections and a variable-width suffix chosen by the producer. Width was not normalized across groups. A leading zero can be part of a producer's chosen identifier. The interface contract therefore describes permitted whitespace trimming but leaves the identifier's interior characters unchanged.

The display label is a separate field intended for an operator's screen. It may contain spaces, mixed capitalization and punctuation. Two entries can have similar descriptions while retaining different route identifiers and destination slots. The lookup API takes the route identifier as a string and returns the matching entry. It does not parse a display label to infer a route key.

TRACE EVENT DICTIONARY
trim records the input and output of surrounding-whitespace handling. split_prefix records the parts produced by a parser's internal hyphen split. numeric_suffix records the numerical value introduced by the candidate transformation. join records the string passed to the manifest lookup. lookup records both the argument and returned slot. emit records the final route-plan fields passed to the preview writer.

These intermediate events were retained by the parser's diagnostic mode during the comparison. The reference matcher does not trust a parser's own match flag; it compares the emitted output with the reference independently. The true/false flags shown with the selected traces are the comparison decisions attached to those traces in the archive, not a substitute for the target strings themselves.

MANIFEST LOOKUP SEMANTICS
The lookup service uses exact string equality on its key field. It has no alias mapping between A-007 and A-7 or between B-004 and B-4. Both members of each pair exist in their respective authored manifests. A successful lookup indicates that the requested key exists, not that the parser requested the key belonging to the incoming source row. The returned destination slot is stored with the route plan as a separate field.

SOURCE ROW SERIALIZATION
The row parser reads a quoted text field for source_id. The archive stores the original field including surrounding spaces so that the trim event can be compared with its input. The leading zeroes in the selected examples were present in the source text; they were not added by a spreadsheet viewer or lost during export. The fixture files use the same text serialization for both builds.

The package description field in mf-059 is document box and in mf-060 is sample kit. Those strings make the rows readable in a route preview but are not used to determine the target. The output slot labels east-07/east-70 and north-04/north-40 are fictional store labels. They are kept distinct to make the final plan's destination visible in the comparator artifact.

PACKAGE DIFFERENCE RECORD
Cedar passes the trimmed source string directly to lookup. Birch adds a helper that parses a numeric-looking suffix and rejoins it to the prefix. The destination adapter and serializer package identifiers are identical between the builds. This manifest describes the change actually traced for the selected cases. No optimization of the dispatcher or rewriting of manifest keys is listed as part of the candidate package.

The diagnostic log preserves the original source_id next to the transformed lookup key. Consequently an operator inspecting the route-plan artifact can see both the input label and the emitted target. The preview writer does not repair their relationship. Its job is to serialize output fields and report whether the plan was stored in the local fixture directory.

VERSIONED CONTRACT ATTACHMENT
Contract revision 5 was attached to the benchmark pack before execution. There is no alternate rule in the request permitting numerical equivalence for suffixes. The scorer's interpretation of leading zeroes therefore follows the attached string contract. This is an authored internal interface, not a claim about how unrelated barcode systems or real warehouses assign their identifiers.

The trace ends at preview output. No dispatch event, inventory mutation, correction transaction or later successful candidate run appears in these selected records. The appendix supplies field semantics and package context while leaving the reference-match counts and observed target values unchanged.

Birch wrong_target_count=2; runner_exception_count=0.

findings.claim: 錯配的具體機制是 Birch 將前導零尾碼數值化，造成既有但錯誤的目標及儲位。

Manifest entries: A-007 -> slot east-07; A-7 -> slot east-70.
numeric_suffix -> 4; join -> "B-4"

findings.claim: 91毫秒的改善僅是小型元件預覽量測，不能抵銷錯配，也不足以預測實際批次風險。

evidence.quote: Median parser duration: Cedar 145 ms; Birch 91 ms.
Timing is a separate diagnostic measure and is not a waiver of identifier preservation.
does not estimate the population frequency of leading-zero identifiers.

limitations: 只有60個作者編寫的情境；未涵蓋所有識別碼格式或實際批次頻率。
未提供修正後 Birch 建置或其重新基準結果。
沒有重複量測分布或信賴區間，故91毫秒改善的穩定性未知。
next_steps: 維持 parser_default=Cedar；不要執行明日批次的設定變更。
移除 Birch 的 numeric-suffix canonicalisation，保持僅修剪周邊空白。
以相同凍結參考檔對修正版重跑，確認逐案60/60 reference match，並附上新比較紀錄後再審。
