source-binding-manifest.json: not captured by export schema 4.
output-receipt.json: present; artifact name, digest and archive-acceptance time only.
expected-r7-output-digest.txt: no reference artifact supplied.

Catalog repository inventory includes immutable source files for R6 and R7. The R7 file adds a connector-inspection column while retaining the table schema accepted by the renderer. The export configuration refers to /catalog/current, a mutable pointer. The archive does not retain the pointer target or cache contents resolved at H17's start time.

TIMELINE
2026-08-24 17:00: request form for H17 signed with label R7.
2026-08-25 03:00: H17 started; effective table-binding revision not recorded.
2026-08-25 03:04: output accepted by archive; receipt stored.
2026-08-26 10:00: repository maintenance log records /catalog/current pointing to R7 at that time. It contains no earlier pointer-history entry.
2026-09-01: H17 output body expired; cover preview and metadata remain under longer retention.
2026-09-08: review request opened for the proposed report sentence.

Archive steward note: "The retained cover image is not a copy of the equipment tables. We have no H17 table-input snapshot or full output body in this archive."
Build-record request BR-H17 seeks the deployed export configuration and any independent binding metadata. Its status is pending; no result is attached. A later export using today's pointer would be a new artifact, not the missing original H17 body. This index does not establish whether another owner retained an independent copy elsewhere.

ARCHIVE INVENTORY FIELD GUIDE
An inventory entry records the artifact name, storage class, creation event, retention class and current availability. Present means the file is available in the reviewed archive. Not captured means that the export build did not write that artifact into the archive. Expired means a previously stored body reached its configured retention deadline. These availability states describe this archive, not every possible copy held by another person or system.

For H17, the signed form and job events belong to the metadata class. The cover image belongs to preview storage. The generated PDF belonged to body storage. The resolved table input and source-binding manifest have no creation events because schema 4 did not capture them. Re-exporting the existing archive index would return the same metadata entries, rather than generate missing historical input files.

CATALOG POINTER RECORDS
The repository stores R6 and R7 under immutable versioned names and exposes /catalog/current as a convenience pointer. The maintenance log entry on 26 August records the pointer at that moment. It is not an audit history of every earlier target. The H17 job started the previous day, and the reviewed archive lacks a pointer-resolution event for that start time.

A table adapter may read the pointer when opening a source or use a worker-local cached table according to its configured mode. The effective mode and cache identity were not recorded in the retained H17 queue event. A repository file's current existence does not supply the missing cache snapshot. The build-record request exists to seek any separately retained configuration evidence; its pending status supplies no answer about what will be found.

VERSIONED SOURCE CONTENT SUMMARY
Both R6 and R7 use the row structure understood by the renderer. Their equipment descriptions and quantities are available in the versioned repository files, and R7 adds connector-inspection entries accepted by that structure. The review packet does not reproduce a row from H17's output with which to compare those versioned inputs. A schema-compatible render could complete without its event record naming the revision used.

The versioned source files are not themselves output artifacts. A regenerated PDF from one of them would have a new generation event and potentially different layout or metadata. The archive index gives no basis for identifying such a later file as the original H17 body merely because its cover carries the same label. Original-artifact identity would need a connection to the retained artifact record, such as a matching original copy, as well as content inspection for the report's claim.

RETENTION TIMELINE DETAIL
The PDF body was accepted on 25 August and expired on 1 September under the seven-day body policy. Metadata and the cover preview remain under their 60-day policies. The inventory was inspected on 8 September, after body expiration. The differing retention periods explain why a report drafter can still see the cover banner and receipt while being unable to open the table pages from this archive.

The body-expiration entry references the generated artifact identifier. It does not mark the artifact as incorrect or corrupted. The absence of the body at review time is a storage-state fact. The packet contains no content inspection performed before expiration that could independently establish which revision supplied the equipment rows.

OPEN RECORD REQUEST
BR-H17 names the export build's effective configuration and any independent binding metadata as requested materials. Its status is pending and its response field is empty. The request does not state that such material is guaranteed to exist. If a later response is obtained it would be a new source attachment requiring its own date and provenance; no such response is silently included in this longer variant.

The archive steward's note is limited to the reviewed archive. It does not certify the absence of a downloaded copy, another team's attachment or an independent backup elsewhere. It also does not promise that any of those will be recoverable. The packet currently provides neither a full body nor a resolved input snapshot with which to certify the proposed historical table-content statement.

documents.title: Export queue configuration and catalog file register
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Configuration context for the internal handover exporter.
The export queue accepts a request form containing a title, a cover label, an intended catalog revision and a table-input location. The renderer places the cover label on page 1. A separate data adapter reads equipment rows from the configured input location. The queue does not require that the cover label be computed from those rows.

The catalog repository has two versioned files relevant to the review: R6 and R7. Both contain equipment identifiers, descriptions, quantities and location fields. R7 additionally provides connector-inspection entries in a column accepted by the current schema. The repository retains both files. Their existence establishes available source versions, not which one H17's adapter read.

The normal job configuration uses the /catalog/current pointer. The adapter can also use a cached table file supplied by the worker process. The retained queue event does not record whether its read used a fresh pointer resolution or the worker cache. The source-binding instrumentation planned for schema 5 was not present in H17's schema 4 record.

The queue stores output page count and archive acceptance independently of content verification. It sends no equipment order, inventory mutation or external message. Its output is a PDF used for an internal handover exercise. The packet contains no subsequent signed row-by-row review of H17 and no real equipment or personnel data.

QUEUE REQUEST LIFECYCLE
The report owner submits a form containing the document title, cover label, intended source revision and input location. The queue assigns a job identifier and stores that form as submitted. A worker reads the queued request, opens the configured table input and renders the document. The archive adapter receives the resulting body, returns a receipt, and the queue records completion.

These stages have separate data fields. The intended revision describes the request. The cover label is display text. The input location tells the data adapter where to obtain rows. A resolved binding record, if captured, would identify what that adapter actually opened. Schema 4 records the first three kinds of input but does not retain the resolved row snapshot or immutable binding identity for H17.

WORKER CACHE SETTINGS
The worker can retain a parsed table between jobs to avoid reparsing an unchanged file. Its effective configuration determines when the cache is refreshed. The retained H17 event lacks the effective cache mode and cache source identifier. The presence of caching as an available mechanism does not establish that it supplied H17's rows, and the absence of a cache field does not establish that the worker read the current pointer afresh.

The worker logs in this packet record job lifecycle events rather than individual file-open operations. A completed job event consequently does not reveal whether the adapter used a cached table or a newly opened versioned file. The record contains no diagnostic trace from which to choose between those paths. This appendix describes the interface capability and recorded fields, not a reconstruction of the missing run-time behavior.

CATALOG MAINTENANCE ROLES
The catalog maintainer publishes immutable revisions. A separate convenience-pointer maintenance action can select a revision for /catalog/current. The report owner selects the desired label on the export request. The renderer reads its configured input location. Those roles can participate in the same workflow without their records becoming interchangeable. The source repository log retained in this packet documents one pointer observation after H17, not the worker's earlier file-open event.

TABLE SCHEMA COMPATIBILITY
The renderer expects equipment identifier, description, quantity and location columns and permits an additional inspection column. Both relevant source revisions are compatible with this shape. A row can be paginated and displayed even when the lifecycle record has no catalog revision field. Schema compatibility is therefore recorded as an input-format property; it is not a content comparison with the request owner's approved revision.

The R7 connector-inspection entries distinguish source content that a reviewer might look for in a recovered table copy. The retained cover preview has no table rows, so those entries are not observable there. The packet also contains no later handwritten transcription of H17's equipment pages. The source-file register lists available revisions but does not supply a surrogate observation of the missing output.

OUTPUT PUBLICATION
After rendering, the archive adapter assigns a body-storage location and stores a receipt with the artifact name and digest. The preview worker saves page 1 in a different storage class. The weekly report drafter has access to the metadata and preview interfaces. Access to those surviving interfaces does not imply that the expired body can still be opened through the same archive path.

Content-review tasks, when separately requested, can attach findings to an artifact record. They are not automatically created by every successful render. H17's archive index contains no completed content-review attachment. The blank evidence field in the weekly report remains part of a drafting process, not a validation result produced by the queue.

CHANGE REGISTER
A planned schema 5 addition would capture immutable source-binding metadata with each export. The planning entry is not a deployed measurement for H17. No statement here claims that the planned feature has run, that it would recover the original body, or that a later job using it would prove the content of an earlier unrecorded binding. The supplied queue configuration remains the schema 4 context recorded in the short packet.

documents.title: Handover report draft and retention operations log
documents.text:
SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Invented report-drafting and archive operations records.
The weekly handover report has an open evidence field beside the proposed H17 catalog sentence. The drafting assistant copied "Catalog R7" from the retained cover preview into a note. A reviewer requested the job record and archive inventory before signing the statement. The evidence field remains unsigned.

Archive retention log:
Metadata and receipts: retain 60 days.
Cover previews: retain 60 days.
Generated PDF bodies: retain 7 days.
Resolved table input snapshots: capture disabled in schema 4.
The H17 body-expiration event was an ordinary scheduled retention operation. The log contains no renderer failure, emergency deletion or corruption finding for H17.

The archive receipt records receipt_id=archive-H17-004, artifact=handover-H17.pdf, digest=demo-h17-6e42 and accepted_at=2026-08-25T03:04:00Z. It lists no table row, catalog revision or inspection result. The cover preview is stored separately from the full PDF body and remains accessible after body expiration.

The report review has not recovered another copy or completed a new reconstruction. No report signature, source lookup, contact or archive restoration is performed by this packet. The reviewer is asked to assess the evidence currently supplied and identify a justified verification path for the unresolved content question.

REPORT DRAFTING WORKFLOW
The weekly report has a section for completed export jobs and a separate section for claims that require content verification. Its draft includes the H17 job identifier, archive receipt and proposed sentence about catalog R7. The evidence cell allows a reviewer to link a retained artifact or inspection result. Copying the cover label into a drafting note does not create such a result; the cell remains unsigned in the supplied record.

The draft history shows the sentence was added after the writer opened the surviving cover preview. The writer did not record opening table pages or comparing equipment rows with the approved source. A reviewer subsequently requested the retained job record and archive index. The packet includes those requested records but no recovered PDF body or completed row comparison.

RETENTION JOB OPERATIONS
The archive retention process selects expired body objects by their storage-class expiration time. It leaves metadata, receipts and cover previews under their own policies. Each expiration event records artifact identifier, retention class and completion time. It does not assess whether a report sentence about the artifact is true. The ordinary H17 expiration event has no attached corruption or content-error finding.

A metadata query can still return an expired body's artifact name, digest, page count and original acceptance time. That response does not contain the body bytes. The preview query can return the independently stored first-page image. The interfaces therefore present different retained parts of a once-complete export. Their availability can be described without inferring the content of pages that are no longer stored in this archive.

RECEIPT FIELD DEFINITIONS
receipt_id identifies the archive service's acceptance record. artifact names the uploaded file. digest copies the file identifier calculated at upload. accepted_at is the time the service accepted the artifact. The receipt schema has no catalog_revision, source_row_count or row_validation field. Absence of those fields is a limitation of the record, not a failed content check represented by a false value.

The same receipt remains after body expiration because it belongs to metadata storage. It can help identify an independently found copy, but the packet includes no such copy. The archive operator has not performed a restoration in the supplied review record. A restoration request would require a source holding the body; the metadata record alone is not a backup of its content.

DRAFT REVIEW STATUS
The proposed weekly sentence is under review. The job-completion entry itself is supported by the retained completed status and receipt. The table-revision evidence field has no attached inspection. The report contains no final signature, distribution event or statement that another reviewer already certified the equipment tables. This status permits the current reviewer to evaluate the sentence without assuming somebody else settled it off-record.

The reviewer has not been asked to run a new export in this packet. A later export from the current catalog pointer would create a new job identifier, new output body and new receipt. It could provide evidence about that later configuration and source, but its results would need to be described with their own provenance. No new replay result is supplied as part of this longer fixture.

RECORD REQUEST HANDOVER
The build-record request BR-H17 is listed as open. The handover names effective configuration and binding metadata as the requested materials but supplies no promised delivery date or guarantee of existence. No operator has reported an independent downloaded PDF, archived attachment or cold-storage body. Their possible existence elsewhere remains outside the reviewed inventory rather than being silently assumed absent or present.

The fictional report concerns internal equipment-list content only. It contains no real inventory instruction, procurement authorization, medical record or legal certification. All records in this appendix describe the same completed export, its surviving metadata and the open review. They introduce no hidden row observation that determines whether H17 used R6, R7 or another effective table input.

FILING CONVENTIONS
The report folder uses separate subfolders for draft prose, source attachments and reviewer sign-off records. Attachment filenames retain their originating job or request identifier. A cover preview is filed under previews, while an archive receipt is filed under metadata. A reviewer note records the date on which an attachment was inspected. The convention allows a later reviewer to distinguish a document drafted on 8 September from a source generated on 25 August without changing either source. A pending record request is filed under requests and carries its request identifier; it is moved into the attachment index only when a response is actually received.

SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Configuration context for the internal handover exporter.

SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. Configuration context for the internal handover exporter.
The export queue accepts a request form containing a title, a cover label, an intended catalog revision and a table-input location. The renderer places the cover label on page 1. A separate data adapter reads equipment rows from the configured input location. The queue does not require that the cover label be computed from those rows.

The catalog repository has two versioned files relevant to the review: R6 and R7. Both contain equipment identifiers, descriptions, quantities and location fields. R7 additionally provides connector-inspection entries in a column accepted by the current schema. The repository retains both files. Their existence establishes available source versions, not which one H17's adapter read.

The normal job configuration uses the /catalog/current pointer. The adapter can also use a cached table file supplied by the worker process. The retained queue event does not record whether its read used a fresh pointer resolution or the worker cache. The source-binding instrumentation planned for schema 5 was not present in H17's schema 4 record.

The queue stores output page count and archive acceptance independently of content verification. It sends no equipment order, inventory mutation or external message. Its output is a PDF used for an internal handover exercise. The packet contains no subsequent signed row-by-row review of H17 and no real equipment or personnel data.

accounting: Actual workload counts each shared generation once. Standalone arm pipelines count each dependency once per case/replicate, including initial and update; arm totals overlap and MUST NOT be summed. Judge/calibration cost included in whole-run actual total and shown separately. Joint prose+state generator is charged in full to either standalone arm; not optimized pure-prose production cost.
limitations: Synthetic mechanism study, not statistical equivalence; repeated rental samples share cases and are not independent users.
Shared source-only memory generation/update, with each arm's prior answer separately retained. Does not measure full assistant-history compaction.
Oracle has preregistered gold document IDs and is a diagnostic bound, not a deployable retriever.
Two document lengths and one sample per retrieval cell cannot establish a general crossover curve.
Calibration uses known errors and a bundled prompt+visibility change, not held-out judge accuracy or a visibility-only causal estimate.
CLI costs exclude parent/subagent authoring, reviews and documentation; processed tokens are not billing/quota.
